bearings.paper_claim: Acting greedily on current value estimates without exploration can lock onto suboptimal actions. On the 10-armed testbed (2000 independent problems, 1000 steps each), the greedy method averages about 1 reward per step against a best possible of about 1.54, and epsilon-greedy does better in the long run. Planning on an incorrect model is likely to compute a suboptimal policy (Sec. 8.3); planning uses a model, learning from experience uses observed interactions (Sec. 8.1).
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 2.2-2.3, pp. 27-30; Sec. 8.1, pp. 159-161; Sec. 8.3 (When the Model Is Wrong)
bearings.system_side: fec/engine/optimize.py allocates a CU budget (default $2.5M in $500 increments, with a per-member cap PMAX) by lazy greedy on modeled marginals of flip_value. The loop stops at the budget or when no positive marginal remains, so spend can fall short of the pot. It has no exploration term. observations is an empty list reserved for real outcomes. It replans after a modeled defection threshold is crossed (the conversions list), so it is not a one-shot plan. In RL terms it is greedy exploitation of a modeled response with no feedback from observed outcomes.
bearings.code_ref: fec/engine/optimize.py:3-12 (docstring), 26 (BUDGET and INC defaults), 58 (observations), 127-150 (greedy loop and modeled conversion replanning)
bearings.transfer_conditions: Exploration pays only if the same allocation repeats and outcomes are observed and fed back. Per-cycle CU outcomes are sparse and confounded, so a bandit layer would learn slowly. The transferable point holds: the optimum is exact only for the model, not for the world.
bearings.verifier_note: Book numbers verified: 2000 problems, 1000 steps, about 1 versus about 1.54. Corrected: the pot is not always fully spent; the optimizer is not one-shot because it replans on modeled conversions; the only-as-good-as-the-model wording is paraphrase, supported by Sec. 8.3 rather than quoted. Greedy is called lazy greedy in the code, not CELF; the two are close but the label should match the code.

bearings.paper_claim: Greedy contextual-bandit policies maximize immediate clicks and ignore long-term effects; an MDP lifetime-value policy (Theocharous et al.) beat greedy on the LTV metric, while greedy won on CTR. In the illustrative Figure 16.8, CTR is 0.35 and LTV is 1.5.
bearings.system_side: The objective at optimize.py line 86 is total_winnability, the sum of flip_value over issues for a single run. The printed objective is labelled expected weighted flips (line 209). The objective is single-run and does not model multi-cycle carry-over. I did not check flip_model or money_response for cross-cycle memory, so the claim that money has no modeled effect on next cycle's receptivity, relationship or stance is confirmed only for the optimizer itself.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Holds only if repeated CU giving to the same member changes later responsiveness. That is untested here. Per D-025 it must not be phrased as access or closeness. Any multi-cycle objective needs owner authorization and a second-path reproduction (DE-062).
bearings.verifier_note: Book passage and figures verified. The system side is narrowed to what optimize.py shows: a single-run objective. The cross-cycle claim about the wider model was not verified.

bearings.paper_claim: Before deploying a new policy, Adobe (Theocharous et al.) estimated its value from data logged under other policies, using high-confidence off-policy evaluation with probabilistic improvement guarantees. Logs: about 200,000 interactions from a campaign that randomly offered one of 7 offers, and about 4,000,000 interactions over 12 offers. The test set was real interactions served by a random policy.
bearings.system_side: outcome_contract.py scores frozen predictors by Spearman: seed_prob against new cosponsorship gain (H1), and pressure_mult against the absolute tier movement (H2). Verdict bars: PASS at 0.20 or above, DIRECTIONAL from 0.10 to 0.20, INDICTED at -0.10 or below. Minimum: 60 days and at least 150 members with a positive cosponsorship delta (the movers count in code). The protocol text instead says 150 members with any delta. The contract ranks frozen predictors; it does not estimate the value of a counterfactual policy. The engaged-only contact arm is marked NOT_IMPLEMENTED_NO_CONTACT_CONTRACT.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Off-policy estimates for alternative allocations need logged actions with known or estimable propensities and overlap. I did not confirm that funding and contact are logged without propensities beyond the missing contact contract. The claim that real assignment is strategic and near-deterministic is the analyst's assertion and has no support in the code I read. Any such estimate stays UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it (DE-062).
bearings.verifier_note: Book passage and Adobe figures verified. Repo side: H1, H2 and bars verified. Corrected: H2 uses absolute tier movement; the movers minimum counts positive cosponsorship deltas, which differs from the protocol text; the propensity-logging absence was not fully verified; the near-deterministic assignment claim is unsupported.
